title: Faith under pressure
hook: They left Bilal in the burning sun. He kept saying one word: One.

screens.text: **They left him out in the burning sun.** Bilal had no tribe to protect him. Whatever they did, he kept repeating one word: *Ahad, Ahad*. One. One.

**Going public had a cost.** The first seven to show their Islam openly included the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Bilal, 'Ammar and his mother Sumayyah. Believers with no tribe to protect them were tortured in the sun [Ibn Majah 150].
bubbles: Bilal, enslaved at the time, never gave in [Ibn Majah 150]. Abu Bakr later bought his freedom [Qalam ep. 37].

cards.back: Enslaved, unprotected, and tortured in the sun. His answer was **tawhid** in one word: *Ahad*, One [Ibn Majah 150].
'Ammar's mother. She was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to give up Islam, and is honoured as Islam's first martyr [SeekersGuidance; Qalam ep. 37; Yaqeen].
Under torture, he said what they demanded. Keep going to see how Allah answered.

screens.text: **Forced words, a firm heart.** 'Ammar came to the Prophet ﷺ in tears. Commentators connect this verse to him: Allah excuses *"one who is forced [to renounce his religion] while his heart is secure in faith"* [Q 16:106, Saheeh Intl.; Qalam ep. 37].
Nobody was spared, not even him.

events.title: The first seven
events.text: A few believers show their Islam openly [Ibn Majah 150].

events.title: The unprotected suffer
events.text: Those with no tribe behind them are tortured in the sun [Ibn Majah 150].

events.title: Sumayyah
events.text: Killed for refusing to give up Islam: the first martyr [SeekersGuidance; Yaqeen].

events.title: He's attacked too
events.text: Waste dumped on his back in prayer; choked with a cloth [Bukhari 240; Bukhari 3856].

events.title: Khabbab asks for help
events.text: He's told that believers before them endured worse, and Allah will complete this religion [Bukhari 3852].

screens.text: **He wasn't spared either.** While he prostrated at the Ka'bah, men dumped a camel's waste on his back, and his daughter Fatimah cleared it away [Bukhari 240]. Another time a man choked him with a cloth until Abu Bakr pushed him off [Bukhari 3856].
bubbles: When Khabbab, who was being tortured, asked him to pray for relief, he said believers before them had endured worse, and Allah would complete this religion [Bukhari 3852].

screens.prompt: Why does the verse about 'Ammar matter so much?

options.text: Allah judges the heart, not words forced out of someone under torture
options.feedback: Right. 'Ammar's heart never left Islam. Allah knew it and excused him [Q 16:106].

options.text: It means faith doesn't need to show in actions
options.feedback: Not quite. It's about being forced. Without force, faith shows in prayer and character.
Not quite. The verse excuses the one forced while the heart stays firm in faith.

screens.text: **Firm, and safe.** You may face pressure too: teasing, cold shoulders, family anger. Allah sees your heart, and nobody asks you to put yourself in danger to prove your faith. {teen}If you're under 18 and things at home get hard, talk to {{mentor.name}}.{/teen}
bubbles: If you're ever unsafe at home, your safety comes first. Tell your mentor, or call for help.

screens.situation: Aaliyah's coworkers tease her every day about her prayer breaks. Today someone hid her prayer mat "as a joke". She dreads going in.

options.text: Tell them calmly it's not okay, and talk to her manager or {{mentor.name}} if it keeps happening
options.feedback: Yes. Patience doesn't mean silence. Calm firmness and asking for help go together.

options.text: Stop praying at work so the teasing stops
options.feedback: Not quite. The prayers are still due. Her mentor can help her find a calmer way to pray at work.

options.text: Put up with it silently forever; suffering is part of faith
options.feedback: Not quite. She doesn't have to accept mistreatment. Bilal endured what he couldn't escape; she can ask for help.

People mock my faith at work. What can I do?

steps: When something feels heavy today, say *Ahad* (One) quietly to yourself
If anyone is giving you a hard time about your faith, tell one person you trust

screens.text: They held on with one word: One. Allah sees the heart, and He never asks you to face harm alone.
Next episode: persecuted at home, a group of Muslims crosses the sea to a Christian king.

check.prompt: What did Bilal keep saying while he was tortured?

options.feedback: Right. He held on to the oneness of Allah [Ibn Majah 150].
Not quite. He kept repeating Ahad, Ahad: One, One [Ibn Majah 150].

check.prompt: What does Q 16:106 say about someone forced to deny their faith?

options.text: They're excused if their heart stays firm in faith
options.feedback: Right. Commentators connect it to 'Ammar, who was forced under torture.

options.text: They have left Islam, no matter what
options.feedback: Not quite. The verse excuses one who is forced while the heart stays secure in faith.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The first seven to show their Islam publicly were the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr, 'Ammar and his mother Sumayyah, Suhayb, Bilal and al-Miqdad. The Prophet ﷺ was protected through Abu Talib and Abu Bakr through his people; the rest were seized and tortured in the sun, and Bilal would only say "Ahad, Ahad" [Ibn Majah 150, Hasan Sahih].
- Sumayyah was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to give up Islam: the first martyr in Islam [SeekersGuidance; Qalam ep. 37; Yaqeen].
- 'Ammar, under torture, said what they demanded and came to the Prophet ﷺ in tears; commentators connect Q 16:106 to him (the one forced while the heart is secure in faith) [Q 16:106; Qalam ep. 37]. Say "commentators connect".
- Camel waste was dumped on his back while he prostrated, and Fatimah removed it [Bukhari 240]; 'Uqbah choked him with a cloth while he prayed until Abu Bakr pushed him away [Bukhari 3856].
- Khabbab asked him to pray for relief; he said believers before them had endured worse and that Allah would complete this religion [Bukhari 3852].
- Bilal was enslaved; Abu Bakr bought his freedom [Qalam ep. 37]. (scholar question Q40)

**Likely questions**
- *"Didn't he tell 'Ammar's family to be patient, promising them Paradise?"* That report is in collections outside the six this program uses; say "the early biographers report" at most, and don't quote it as a hadith.
- *"Was Bilal a slave?"* Yes, at the time. Slavery existed everywhere then; Abu Bakr bought his freedom, and Bilal became one of Islam's most honoured Companions (the first caller to prayer comes in seerah-24). Don't claim slavery is acceptable today or that Islam abolished it in one stroke; detail goes to the imam. (scholar question Q40)
- *"What if I'm pressured to hide my faith?"* Respond with care. Many converts aren't public yet, and that's understood. The verse about 'Ammar shows Allah judges the heart under force; how it applies to the convert's own situation (family, work) is for the imam. If there's danger, safety rule first.
- *"People mock my faith at work."* Calm, firm boundaries; document and report harassment to a manager or HR; lean on the mentor. Legal questions go to a professional.

**Escalate:** any danger at home or at work (safety rule: crisis resources, offer to alert someone the convert chooses, never only the imam queue); whether a convert may hide their Islam in a specific situation (personal ruling); detailed slavery questions (Q40).

**Don't**
- No graphic torture detail: don't describe chain mail, burning or the iron combs and saws in Bukhari 3852.
- Never present torture or abuse as something a convert must endure to prove faith.
- Don't quote the "family of Yasir" saying as hadith.
- Don't picture the Prophet ﷺ or any Companion.

- [Bukhari 240](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:240) (Sahih): camel waste on his back; Fatimah.
- [Bukhari 3856](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3856) (Sahih): 'Uqbah chokes him; Abu Bakr intervenes.
- [Bukhari 3852](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3852) (Sahih): Khabbab's request.
- [SeekersGuidance (Zaynab Ansari), *Amazing Muslim Women: Sumayyah*](https://seekersguidance.org/articles/history/amazing-muslim-women-sumayyah/): the first martyr.
- [Yaqeen Institute, *How Muhammad ﷺ Confronted Hate…*](https://yaqeeninstitute.org/read/paper/how-muhammad-confronted-hate-and-became-the-most-influential-person-in-history): Sumayyah; persecution in Makkah.
- [Qalam Institute, *The Sīrah Podcast*, ep. 37, The torture of the early Muslims](https://www.qalaminstitute.org/2013/02/seerah-life-of-the-prophet-the-torture-suffering-of-the-early-muslims-in-makkah/): Sumayyah, 'Ammar, Bilal freed by Abu Bakr.
